I. GENERAL
Services and protection for women and children constitute a series of activities that must be pursued continuously, sustainably, in a directed manner and guarantee the growth and development of children physically, mentally, spiritually and socially so as to realize a good life and be able to become potential successors of the nation, resilient, of noble character and possessing a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also guarantees that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the first objective of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect all the people and the entire homeland of Indonesia.
Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on December 10, 1948 and ratified CEDAW (Convention on The Elimination of All Forms Of Discrimination Against Women) with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of all forms of Discrimination against women, thus is obliged to comply with these provisions.
Likewise in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially www.jdih.manggaraibaratkab.go.id the Government, and the said Law also constitutes a legal umbrella for all the formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination. Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women of 1999, it is stated that women as Mothers of the nation and children as the next generation of the nation who are creatures of God Almighty must therefore be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.
From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because such acts constitute crimes against human existence.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is West Manggarai Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Manggarai Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of West Manggarai.
4. Woman is a person who has reproductive organs that can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth and breastfeeding.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb.
6. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
7. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness or causes death.
8. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
9. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual relations, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
10. Economic violence is neglect of family members in the form of not providing a proper living care and maintenance.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
www.jdih.manggaraibaratkab.go.id
12. Services for women and children are actions that must be immediately carried out including protection provided to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or completed occurrence of violence against victims.
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Community, the Police, the Prosecutor's Office, the Court, social institutions or other parties who know or hear of the impending or completed occurrence of violence against women.
14. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
16. Women and Children Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as P3A is an institution providing services to victims of violence in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
17. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
18. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
19. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband-wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children.
www.jdih.manggaraibaratkab.go.id
20. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

REGARDING
SERVICES AND PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

CHAPTER IV
RIGHTS OF VICTIMS
Article 5
Every victim has the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling both from individuals, groups or institutions whether Government or Non-Government.
www.jdih.manggaraibaratkab.go.id

CHAPTER VI
ASSISTANCE
Article 11
Assistance is carried out by persons or bodies/institutions that have the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence and have cooperated with P3A.

1.9.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, the regulation defines “kekerasan seksual” (Pasal 1 angka 9) as sexual harassment and forced sexual relations, including acts “untuk tujuan komersial dan/atau tujuan tertentu” (for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes). However, the text does not explicitly mention “perbudakan seksual” (sexual slavery) or “eksploitasi seksual” as distinct forms, nor does it define trafficking/sexual exploitation separately. The retrieved English candidates did include the key definition (Article 1(9)), and the judge’s rationale—that sexual exploitation/sexual slavery are not explicitly included as distinct concepts—matches what the Indonesian actually says. Therefore the disagreement is best explained by the golden label being too broad for this document’s wording.

4.4.rationale: The original Indonesian text explicitly includes prevention through education. Pasal 4 ayat (1) huruf b states: “Melakukan pendidikan tentang nilai-nilai anti kekerasan terhadap perempuan dan anak” (conduct education on anti-violence values toward women and children). The retrieved candidate passage [4.4-8] contains this exact provision in English, and the judge correctly cited it to answer Yes. Since the document clearly provides for education as a prevention measure, the golden label of No appears incorrect.
